title: Halloumi Burgers
subtitle: Grilled halloumi with roasted red pepper and avocado
excerpt: Thick slices of halloumi are grilled until golden and squeaky, then served in a roll or flatbread with roasted red pepper, smashed avocado, and mint. These are filling and fast. The halloumi needs a very hot pan to colour well without going rubbery.
sourceNotes: Halloumi is a Cypriot cheese with a high melting point, making it ideal for grilling. Halloumi burgers became popular in UK cafes and restaurants through the 2010s as a vegetarian staple.

content.text: Pat the halloumi dry before it goes in the pan. Any moisture will cause it to steam rather than sear. The pan must be very hot and you should not move the halloumi until it releases easily from the pan.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the pan over a high heat. Add the peppers skin-side down.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is blistered and charred. Flip and cook for 1 more minute. Remove and set aside.
Mash the avocado with the garlic and lemon juice. Season with salt. Set aside.
Pat the halloumi slices dry with kitchen paper.
Add the remaining oil to the pan over a high heat. When it is very hot, add the halloumi.
Cook for 2 minutes without moving. Flip when golden. Cook for 2 more minutes on the other side.
Build the burgers: smashed avocado on the base, then halloumi, roasted pepper, and mint. Serve in flatbread, a roll, or on a plate.

items.symptom: The halloumi is rubbery and not golden.
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or slices were too thick.
items.fix: Use higher heat and slice halloumi no thicker than 1.5cm.

items.symptom: The halloumi is sticking to the pan.
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough when the cheese went in.
items.fix: Wait until the oil shimmers, then add the halloumi and do not move it.
